items.title: The Sequence Knowledge - Issue #973: Learning RSI: World Models as Training Grounds for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: World models are presented as training grounds for self-improving agents by generating the consequences of actions. A learned simulator can create experience on demand, which, when combined with task proposal and evaluation systems, forms an improvement machinery. DeepMind's SIMA 2 and Genie 3 offer early examples of this setup. The discussion questions whether this generated experience teaches transferable capabilities. The analysis also touches upon the economic cost of experience generation and the recursive nature of improvement.
items.audio_script: From thesequence.substack.com, The Sequence Knowledge - Issue number nine hundred seventy-three discusses learning reinforcement learning from interacting with world models as training grounds for self-improving agents. DeepMind's work explores using learned simulators to generate the consequences of actions, creating experience on demand which, when integrated with task proposal and evaluation systems, forms an improvement machinery. Early examples of this setup are demonstrated through systems such as SIMA two and Genie three. The discussion examines whether this generated experience imparts transferable capabilities and analyzes the economic cost associated with experience generation and the recursive nature of improvement. This research indicates a pathway for creating agents capable of self-directed skill enhancement through simulated interaction. Future developments will focus on assessing the quality and generality of these self-generated skills.

items.title: Opinion: Moravec’s paradox explains why physical AI needs a sense of touch
items.summary: Moravec's paradox highlights that while intellectual tasks are easy for machines, physical interactions are profoundly difficult. This disconnect arises because human sensory processing evolved to hide complex physical computations below conscious awareness. The point of contact presents a major hurdle for physical AI, as visual systems lack the necessary data to handle real-world resistance. Integrating force and torque sensing allows robots to 'feel' the physical world instead of relying solely on visual predictions. Therefore, grounding physical AI requires integrating precise, real-time sensory feedback into the core hardware architecture.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: Moravec’s paradox explains why physical AI needs a sense of touch." This story examines how Moravec's paradox illustrates the difficulty in achieving physical artificial intelligence due to the gap between intellectual ease and physical interaction. The disconnect stems from the fact that human sensory processing evolved to conceal complex physical computations below conscious awareness, creating a major hurdle for physical AI systems. The physical point of contact proves challenging because visual systems lack the necessary data to process real-world resistance. Integrating force and torque sensing into robotic systems allows them to perceive the physical world directly rather than relying only on visual predictions. Grounding physical AI necessitates incorporating precise, real-time sensory feedback into the fundamental hardware architecture. This shift indicates a direction for advancing physical robotics development.

items.title: GXO and Apptronik plan rollout of up to 1,000 humanoid robots
items.summary: GXO Logistics partnered with Apptronik to develop a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model for deploying humanoid robots in logistics. The collaboration focuses on applying humanoid robots to tasks like goods-to-person picking, case movement, and sortation within warehouse workflows. Joint trials of the Apollo robot in live operations will occur, validating safety and performance against agreed KPIs starting in 2027. If successful, the companies plan a global rollout of up to 1,000 humanoid robots over four years, beginning in North America in late 2027. This initiative aims to leverage physical AI to improve logistics by enabling humanoids to collaborate with existing automation and staff.

This initiative seeks to utilize physical artificial intelligence to enhance logistics by enabling humanoids to work alongside existing automation and personnel. The success of this phased deployment will set a benchmark for physical AI integration in supply chain management.

items.title: Booster T2 targets developers with an open humanoid platform
items.summary: Booster Robotics offers its T2 humanoid as an open platform for developers to build robot intelligence, emphasizing access to APIs and software development kits. The company provides hardware and operating system tools, while focusing on AI models and algorithms through investment. The T2 robot measures 1.4 meters tall, weighs 42 kilograms, and features 31 degrees of freedom with interchangeable end effectors. The platform includes tools like Booster Studio for simulation and deployment, allowing developers control over model behavior. Operational safety and integration largely depend on the customer-supplied software stack and task complexity.

items.title: The hidden reason most robots fail on the factory floor
items.summary: Most robots fail on the factory floor due to a lack of real-world application, as stated by Standard Bots co-founder Evan Beard. Standard Bots designs and assembles its robots in-house, developing the entire robotics stack from hardware to AI. Beard advocates for a coordinated U.S. robotics strategy to advance the industry. Intel is supporting this progress by providing a platform that integrates AI inference, sensing, and real-time control for robotics. Ultimately, the focus of the future of robotics is making these machines functional in the real world.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "The hidden reason most robots fail on the factory floor". This segment examines the primary cause of robot failure on the factory floor, which is attributed to a lack of real-world application. Standard Bots co-founder Evan Beard details that the failure stems from the robots not being adequately tested in practical industrial settings. Standard Bots designs and assembles its robotics systems internally, managing the entire stack from hardware to artificial intelligence. Beard further suggests a coordinated United States robotics strategy is necessary for industry advancement, noting that Intel is contributing to this progress by providing a platform that integrates artificial intelligence inference, sensing, and real-time control for robotics. The future direction for robotics is centered on ensuring these machines achieve functionality within actual operational environments. This focus indicates that practical deployment remains the critical barrier for advancing the artificial intelligence and technology sectors.

items.title: Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
items.summary: Remedy Robotics is developing a robotic system, the N1, to facilitate remote stroke surgery, specifically thrombectomies. The system uses a robotic arm and steerable catheter controlled remotely, aiming to bring specialized care to remote and rural areas. This technology seeks to overcome geographic barriers for patients who need time-critical stroke treatment. Success for telesurgery depends on robust communication infrastructure and optimizing for latency while ensuring patient safety. Researchers are focusing on making remote procedures faster and safer, with the goal of expanding access to emergency stroke care.

The technology aims to overcome geographic barriers for patients requiring time-critical stroke treatment by employing remote operation techniques. Researchers are actively focusing on improving the speed and safety of these remote procedures to expand access to emergency stroke care. This advancement signals a potential shift in the deployment of advanced robotics within critical medical infrastructure.

items.title: Richtech Robotics to unveil AI-powered cleaning system at ISSA Show 2026
items.summary: Richtech Robotics will unveil its Intelligent Cleaning System at the ISSA Show North America 2026 in Las Vegas. This system connects autonomous cleaning robots, camera monitoring, and operational data for intelligent and responsive hygiene management. The system integrates existing indoor CCTV with Dust-E robots to automatically identify and execute targeted cleaning tasks. A centralized dashboard provides facility intelligence, tracking robot locations, records, and alerts for maintenance. Richtech Robotics will also showcase various robots and present on building complete robotics floor care programs.

items.title: Hyundai takes full Boston Dynamics ownership for Atlas push
items.summary: Hyundai Motor Group affiliates and Executive Chair Chung Euisun now own all of Boston Dynamics after acquiring SoftBank’s remaining stake. This acquisition supports Hyundai's goal to achieve an annual production capacity of 30,000 Atlas humanoids by 2028, with initial deployment planned at its Georgia site. The transaction involved Hyundai Glovis, which invested 46.5 billion won, and Hyundai Motor alone. The Atlas robots are initially intended for sorting and transporting automotive parts at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia. Full ownership simplifies funding and deployment coordination for the Atlas development.

The acquisition involved Hyundai Glovis investing forty-six point five billion won and Hyundai Motor separately. These Atlas robots are slated for initial use in sorting and transporting automotive parts at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia, and the full ownership streamlines funding and deployment coordination for Atlas development. This move signals a significant step toward scaling humanoid robotics within the automotive technology sector.

items.title: Welcome, Pelican VL 2.0!
items.summary: Pelican VL 2.0 is an embodied AI foundation model developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X Humanoid). It functions as the brain layer of a robotics system, separate from the physical body or motor controller. The model's Brain Score of 2 out of 10 suggests an early stage of autonomy, warranting a measured evaluation approach. It is being offered as a commercial service, extending beyond the center's own Tiangong ecosystem. The key distinction is separating the foundation model from the motion controller for proper system assessment.

items.title: Welcome, AstraBrain!
items.summary: AstraBrain is an embodied AI software system from Beijing Galbot AI Co., Ltd., powering their humanoid robots rather than being a physical robot itself. Its architecture features a planning component (brain), a body control component (cerebellum), and a connecting bridge module. The system's controller is named AstraBrain WBC, highlighting the separation between the planning and control layers. It achieved a Humanoid.Guide Brain Score of 8 out of 10 and was presented at the World Robot Conference in August 2026. AstraBrain functions as a shared software layer across Galbot's broader robotics lineup.

The system's architecture incorporates a planning component designated as the brain, a body control component referred to as the cerebellum, and a connecting bridge module. The controller for this system is named AstraBrain WBC, emphasizing the distinct separation between the planning and control layers within the design. items.title: Penguin Random House doubles book picking productivity with Locus Robotics
items.summary: Penguin Random House Grupo Editorial is using Locus Robotics to modernize book distribution in its Barcelona operation to handle fragmented and seasonal demand. The company scaled its Locus Robotics deployment from 14 robots to 40, managing nearly 1,000 SKUs, and now handles over one and a half million units monthly. This system increases picking productivity to over 510 units per hour compared to manual methods. The flexible infrastructure allows the operation to scale through demand variability without disruption during major facility transitions. Locus Robotics enabled PRHGE to quickly redeploy its automation fleet during a move to a new facility.

items.title: Robot swarms trained by trial and error in simulation keep working on real robots
items.summary: Reinforcement learning trained robot swarms in simulation reliably perform on physical robots despite the "reality gap." Researchers overcame this by restricting the learning algorithm to choose from a set of tried-and-tested behaviors rather than directly controlling every motor. This method ensures that the learned skills are grounded in real-world constraints rather than simulator quirks. Experiments with 20 e-puck robots showed this approach significantly outperformed other methods. This work bridges the gap between reinforcement learning and reliable swarm robotics for complex real-world tasks.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "Robot swarms trained by trial and error in simulation keep working on real robots". This report details a method used by researchers to ensure the reliable performance of robot swarms when transitioning from simulation to physical hardware. The research involved training reinforcement learning agents in simulation and then deploying these learned skills onto physical robots, addressing the challenge known as the reality gap. To mitigate simulation inaccuracies, the learning algorithm was restricted to selecting from a set of previously tested behaviors instead of directly controlling every motor. Experiments conducted with twenty e-puck robots demonstrated that this approach significantly outperformed other methodologies in achieving complex real-world tasks. This work establishes a pathway for reliable swarm robotics by bridging the gap between simulation-based learning and physical execution. The development suggests a more robust approach for deploying artificial intelligence in complex robotic systems.

items.title: Agile Robots raises $500M to increase production capacity
items.summary: Agile Robots raised $500 million in Series F funding, achieving a valuation of $8.5 billion and total funding of $2 billion. The company builds and deploys various robots, including humanoids, mobile robots, and robotic arms, alongside their associated software and AI models. Funding will be used to increase production capacity and expand the company's presence in key global markets. Agile Robots aims to bring physical AI into industrial production across various sectors like automotive and manufacturing. The company is expanding its production capacity, including a facility in Germany, to meet growing demand.
